notes.title: VR and flat mode – which is easier to play?
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/8826f6692953b1d25c1c2014f2e0e3592213cb1c.jpg[/img]
Friends, we are closely monitoring your feedback and see that you are concerned about the effectiveness of pilots with different ways of immersing themselves in the game (pilots with VR devices and those who will use a monitor).

To be clear: in Aces of Thunder, there is only cockpit view and only realistic control options. There is no “mouse aiming” here – the game was planned from the very beginning as a realistic simulator, where all participants are in equally “adult” conditions.

So we do not think that the “flat” mode (without VR) has any noticeable advantage – rather the opposite. The player in VR is better informed about what is happening around them (contacts are more visible, since all game objects and planes have real dimensions, and the perception of distance in VR is more accurate). Although with a large monitor, a good joystick and sufficient experience, the capabilities of players are quite comparable. Nevertheless, we are studying how different devices can affect the balance and its subjective perception.

We want to assure you that we are studying the necessity of implementing matchmaking taking into account the image output option. We are conducting tests, analysing data and will definitely make a decision that will be fair and convenient for all players. Thank you for your passion and your feedback — every comment helps us improve the game. We're on the same wavelength and will make sure to choose the path that serves the best interests of the majority of players.

notes.title: Aces of Thunder will be playable without VR!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/606ab09f5e926e355cf83fd3deea83e5a5d792d9.jpg[/img]
If you don’t have a VR headset or are yet unsure which one to buy, don’t worry: some time after the release of Aces of Thunder the game will receive an update adding a “flat screen” mode. It will allow all users of PlayStation 5 and PCs powerful enough to run the game to enjoy Aces of Thunder without using VR devices, while retaining the highest levels of realism. For maximum immersion, however, we recommend using a HOTAS and a VR headset.

Aces of Thunder is currently nearing the end of its development, but will be released only when it’s fully ready. Intense PvP battles, challenging solo missions and scenario editor to let your creativity run wild await you.

Subscribe to our social network accounts to keep track on the news, and add Aces of Thunder to your wishlists in Steam and PSN!

notes.title: Anniversary of the La-5’s maiden flight
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/ae793cf74b6be0db443df7915c0c0a981bee77c0.jpg[/img]

On March 21st 1942, the La-5, a fighter aircraft designed by Semyon Lavochkin, took to the skies for the first time. At lower altitudes, this aircraft was capable of fending off Luftwaffe aircraft on equal footing. This prompted the USSR to ramp up its production: a total of 10,000 La-5s were built during WWII.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/77062456cf781e1aaf2e432d4576dcce0227e0b6.jpg[/img]

In Aces of Thunder, you’ll be able to pilot the most advanced version of this fighter — the La-5FN. We’ve also updated our [url=https://acesofthunder.net/en/]official site[/url] — visit it to learn more about the game!

notes.title: Legendary Biplanes: SPAD S.XIII
notes.content:
Welcome, future pilots of Aces of Thunder! Today we’d like to present the French biplane that you’ll be able to fly in the game.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/5e14be1f08f40bd603c44d20f44bf27ca5bf7942.jpg[/img]
[list][*] Cruising speed: 190 km/h
[*] Armament: 2x 7.7 mm synchronized Vickers machine guns
[/list]
Designed by Louis Béchereau, the SPAD S.XIII made its first flight on April 4th 1917 and became the most widely produced fighter of World War I. A total of 8,472 were built.
The SPAD S.XIII is heavy and not very maneuverable, but make use of its strengths — it’s the fastest aircraft in level flight and during dives.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/4a0df3d7c894f2877e9758f4ec050ba84648ba85.jpg[/img]
[i]Did you know?
You may have noticed the unusual exhaust pipes running along the fuselage. They were deliberately designed to be this long to prevent the pilot from being blinded by exhaust flames.[/i]

notes.title: Legendary Biplanes: Sopwith F.1 Camel
notes.content:
We continue to introduce WWI aircraft that will feature in Aces of Thunder. Today, our focus is on the dangerous yet highly effective "Camel"!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/4040f9846942e67cec9c3ed34a5ccdb71e93140c.jpg[/img]
[list]
[*] Cruising speed: 177 km/h
[*] Armament: 2x 7.7 mm synchronized Vickers machine guns
[/list]Designed by Herbert Smith in 1916, the Sopwith Camel features a streamlined fuselage and a distinctive “humpbacked” profile, which earned it the nickname of “Camel”. To improve visibility, special cutouts were made in the middle and along the trailing edge of the upper wing.

In a dogfight, it’s recommended to turn left, as it is noticeably faster than turning right. Be cautious, as at low speeds the aircraft has a tendency to stall into a spin.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/884bfc826c4ba55f245dfae6083e277d6db1eab1.jpg[/img]
[i]Did you know?
During the war, 385 pilots lost their lives in non-combat related flight incidents, while 415 were killed in battles. Despite this, the Sopwith Camel became one of the most successful fighters of its time, with pilots flying it scoring over 1,200 aerial victories.[/i]

notes.title: Legendary Biplanes: Fokker D.VII
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/dc6095082c0b645faaff347f90831684bebb0ac3.jpg[/img]
Last month, we introduced the first WWI plane that is set to appear in Aces of Thunder. Today we’ll talk about its close relative, the Fokker D.VII.
[list]
[*] Cruising speed: 180 km/h
[*] Armament: 2x 7.92 mm synchronized LMG 08/15 Spandau machine guns
[/list]
This more traditionally designed low-wing fighter first took to the skies in 1917. Compared to the D.I, the D.VII is less maneuverable especially at low altitudes, but is more stable at higher altitudes and outperforms many enemy aircraft in terms of characteristics. Famous WWI ace Ernst Udet flew this aircraft and achieved over 60 aerial victories, becoming renowned for his bold and aggressive tactics.

Before engaging in combat, it’s recommended to gain altitude to secure an energy advantage for effective dogfighting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/abfd53fd8a0e6901f77cd7b97dc9d8681a943c81.jpg[/img]
[i]Did you know?
By the end of the war, the D.VII was the primary fighter of the German aerial forces, making up 75% of all aircraft in squadrons. It achieved more victories than any other fighter in WWI.[/i]

notes.title: Legendary Biplanes and Triplanes: Fokker Dr.I
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/8335ba71dfe25a78ff0be429cc1588ad37c14fc2.jpg[/img]
Aces of Thunder takes you back to the era of epic aerial battles between the Entente and Central Powers, where you’ll take control of legendary World War I aircraft such as the SPAD S.XIII or the Fokker Dr.I. These fighters were not only icons of aerial combat but also embodied the technological achievements of their time. With every maneuver, you’ll feel the power of history, and with every takeoff, the wind and freedom beneath your wings.

The low-speed aircraft featured in Aces of Thunder were crafted from wood and fabric and have charming open cockpits. Inside, you’ll find authentic mechanical instruments, springs, and tension cables running through the fuselage to the controls. Unlike World War II aircraft, the machine guns are mounted on the fuselage, rather than concealed within the body.
Though World War I era aircraft were just beginning their journey as combat vehicles, they significantly influenced the course of the war.

[h1]Fokker Dr.I[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/65a370a27e74ce4e42f61ee6eeaad096bbe0578c.jpg[/img]
[list]
[*] Cruising speed: 152 km/h
[*] Armament: 2x 7.92 mm synchronized LMG 08/15 Spandau machine guns
[/list]You’ve likely heard of the German Fokker thanks to the iconic ace pilot Manfred von Richthofen, more commonly referred to as the “Red Baron”. This aircraft was developed by the Fokker company, established by Dutch aircraft designer Anton Fokker. The triplane conducted its first flight on June 25th 1917, and remained in active service until 1918. 
In the game, the Fokker Dr.I is best suited for close combat, as its distinctive three-boom design enhances maneuverability, albeit with reduced stability at higher altitudes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/d4d007ebc9738fcee7f343245c8990563caaa8e2.jpg[/img]
[i]Did you know?
During the triplane’s first combat sortie on the morning of September 1st, it achieved its first victory: Manfred von Richthofen shot down a British RE.8 spotter over the front line. The Fokker Dr.I is frequently referenced in literature and cinema, establishing its reputation as one of history's most renowned fighter aircraft.[/i]

We’ll talk about other aircraft from the First World War in the next updates. Stay tuned!

notes.title: Curtiss SB2C “Helldiver”
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/841be70cb2d99816f9cba750bd6c4809eb673a71.jpg[/img]
In December 1943, the U.S. Navy's Curtiss SB2C, a carrier-based scout-bomber, made its first flight. In honor of this event, we will share some information about this aircraft. 

In Aces of Thunder, the SB2C-4 version is featured – this is the most produced and final modification of the "Helldivers" that participated in World War II. The aircraft entered production in 1944 and played an active role in the massive strike against the Japanese fleet led by the super battleship Yamato. A total of 2,415 units were built.

The "Helldiver" is a fast aircraft: at an altitude of 5 km, it can reach speeds of up to 441 km/h and boasts one of the most impressive weaponry sets in the game. Your arsenal includes 250 lb, 500 lb, and 1000 lb bombs, HVAR rockets, as well as two variants of Mk.13-6 torpedoes. For those who enjoy shooting down unsuspecting enemy fighters, you can equip two suspended 12.7 mm M2 Browning machine guns alongside the two 20 mm AN/M2 wing-mounted cannons. However, keep in mind that this will add 240 kg to the already heavy dive bomber's weight, making it even more challenging to maneuver and maintain a safe speed without entering a spin.

Although the rear hemisphere is covered by a gunner operating a turret with two 7.62 mm Browning machine guns, try to avoid having the enemy behind you – maneuver constantly. When attacking ground and naval targets, don't forget about the air brake, especially during steep dives.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/1209fa5c186441e70f3b7e388013206e22ac13ca.jpg[/img]
In specific missions, you will find two tasks where you can pilot the SB2C-4. In the mission "First Strike," your objective as part of a squadron of "Helldivers" is to conduct a bombing raid on an airfield on Saipan Island. Be warned, interceptors will be coming your way!

In the mission "Second Wave," using your forward armament, you will need to suppress enemy air defenses and artillery. Shore-based guns will attempt to thwart your landing, while agile Japanese A6M3s will oppose American aircraft in the air. Under the cover of P-63A-5 "King Cobras," try to destroy as many ground targets as possible in the first few passes and keep an eye out constantly!
[table noborder=1]
    [tr]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/5719f2080cbc80a5860f885f2116a17fbf1df406.jpg[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/a5d492e4108910200947bb281a6db724e3b7c530.jpg[/img][/th]
        [th][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/b77a17258d87b54f87c4353942b71aa3998cffc7.jpg[/img][/th]
    [/tr]
[/table]
As for the name "Helldiver," it is not related to the aircraft's characteristics. It is a nickname for a waterbird – the Pied-billed Grebe, which inhabits rivers and lakes in North America. It also has another nickname – Water Witch. This bird can dive deeply and stay underwater for a long time. We hope you won’t need that skill in Aces of Thunder.

notes.title: Release in 2025
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/b6e964f801ff215620886a5a8e6b8f95c9e475e2.jpg[/img]
Dear players! In the comments under our posts you ask, “When will the game be released?” We’d like to let you know that Aces of Thunder has been slightly postponed to 2025. While almost everything is currently ready, we’d like a little extra time to polish the game. In addition, we’ve also decided to prepare more content for Aces of Thunder than we initially planned, which we will discuss in more detail later in a separate developer diary. We will definitely announce the exact release date in a separate news article in the early months of next year.

We don’t want to make all of you wait too long, but our goal is to create an interesting, high-quality, diverse and most importantly fun game that everyone will enjoy playing, and to realise that vision we just need a bit more time. Stick around! We’ve got lots of exciting things still to show you all, we’ll share more very soon!

Our deepest thanks for your patience and support o7

notes.title: The Pilot's Tablet – Your Best Friend!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=6npLIHGeDEA;full][/previewyoutube]
When we started developing Aces of Thunder, one of the most important questions we faced was about interacting with the interface in VR. Fortunately, we found an organic immersive solution, as every pilot, in addition to their helmet and parachute, has a knee-mounted tablet!

In virtual reality, a diegetic interface that does not disrupt your immersion in the game world is especially important. All interactions in Aces of Thunder occur using your hands, and selecting options in the menu will be no exception: with one hand, you will hold the pilot's tablet, while with the other, you will perform the necessary actions on it.

Choosing the right aircraft, determining its load, changing the game mode, time of day, weather, and so on – your trusty tablet will help you interact with the game interface!

notes.title: Aces of Thunder: Japan Aviation
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=onvhDdnbFPE;full][/previewyoutube]
Just to remind you, you’ll be able to take the pilot’s seat in each of these aircraft, enjoy an extremely detailed cockpit, and control the aircraft directly from a first-person perspective in VR!

The Japanese Air Force is unimaginable without the carrier-based A6M Zero fighter — the most widespread aircraft of the Imperial Navy that was used throughout the entire war: from skirmishes with Chinese pilots and the strike on Pearl Harbor to desperate kamikaze attacks. The islands were defended from American bombing by the J2M Raiden and Ki-61 Hien fighters, while the D4Y Suisei bombers, with speeds comparable to the Zero, effectively countered the Allied fleet.

These are just the aircraft that will be available in Aces of Thunder at release: in subsequent updates we plan to further expand the game’s aircraft. Stay tuned for more news!

notes.title: Aces of Thunder: USSR Aviation
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=lYjycZr5DuM;full][/previewyoutube]
Welcome to our regular news article, where we show you aircraft that will arrive with the launch of the upcoming realistic flight simulator Aces of Thunder! This time, we’ll touch on the aircraft that were used in the Eastern front.

The addition of the Soviet air force in Aces of Thunder will welcome aircraft that are capable of taking on the wonders of mighty German aircraft. These are the Yak-9, which was also flown by Yugoslav partisans, the lighter and more agile Yak-3, and the somewhat maneuverable La-5N. But it’s impossible not to talk about the earlier IL-2 attack aircraft, as it’s one of the most known aircraft in history, nicknamed by its designers as the “Flying Tank”! This aircraft has bombs that are capable of destroying German armor. 

These aircraft will be immediately unlocked and available to players at the start of Aces of Thunder. Whatever one you want to take into a combat mission in virtual reality is entirely your choice!

notes.title: Take control!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/91a101ced2edc8255af52f7f2ce12139870ff7f7.gif[/img]

A control stick and throttle are the key controls to any aircraft, be it a fighter or an attack aircraft. In Aces of Thunder, you can control your aircraft by using the sticks on the  controller and also take control of the throttle and rudder with literally your own hands! To do this, just reach out with your virtual hands, grab them, and then move the controller in the same way as you would move a control stick while sitting in the cockpit of a real aircraft.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/8de664a94d3a515cdb6b558b53049477fedbbe19.gif[/img]

You can also use the touch of your hands to control the flaps and landing gear — plus, even open the cockpit canopy if it gets too hot in battle!

Use the most immersive and intuitive controls to navigate in the most realistic air battles in Aces of Thunder when it releases on Steam!

notes.title: Aces of Thunder: British Aviation
notes.content:
[video]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/257042012/movie480_vp9.webm[/video]

Per Ardua ad Astra! The Royal Air Force will greet virtual reality pilots with the launch of the Aces of Thunder flight simulator with four renowned aircraft that fought in World War II.

Guarding the shores of Great Britain is the Spitfire, one of the most advanced aircraft of the Battle of Britain, and Typhoons, which joined later, and together, these aircraft supported the Allies during the Normandy landings. The carrier-based Firefly patrolled the coast of Norway and raided Japanese-occupied islands, while the low-flying Mosquito bombarded German-controlled cities, delivering pinpoint strikes on critical targets such as the Gestapo headquarters in Aarhus and Copenhagen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/ed9039cbf904e280f3ef8c134fadc49b0d849e53.jpg[/img]
See you in the next publication!

notes.title: Meet Aces of Thunder, VR flight sim from the makers of War Thunder!
notes.content:
[video]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/257029241/movie480_vp9.webm[/video]
We’re happy to introduce Aces of Thunder, a new flight simulation game that we’re developing for VR devices! Aces of Thunder is a spin-off of the popular online game War Thunder dedicated to aerial battles of legendary aircraft in the most iconic theaters of war.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45107724/ed9039cbf904e280f3ef8c134fadc49b0d849e53.jpg[/img]
On release, over twenty meticulously recreated models will be available instantly: the American P-51 Mustang and P-63 Kingcobra fighters, the German Bf 109 and Fw 190 fighters, the Soviet IL-2 attack aircraft, the British Spitfire fighter and the Japanese A6M3 Zero. You can admire both the interior and exterior of these beauties by walking around them on the airfield.

Flights will take place entirely from within the cockpit, where you can quite literally grab the controls with your hands and spin a turn. We did everything to recreate the controls of each aircraft as realistically and accurately as possible while maintaining comfort for VR players.
